## Introduction

### Overview 
This session introduces [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) and helps to get started with Quarto.


### Learning goals
In this session, you will learn:

- Basics of Quarto (syntax and formats)

Quarto is the next-generation version of R Markdown that allows to combine prose, code, 
results. Quarto is not limited to single programming language but is available in R, Python, 
Julia and Observable. Here, we will learn to use it in RStudio.

Quarto documents are reproducible and support different output formats 
such as PDFs, Word files, presentations.

**Advantages of using Quarto:**

1. Communicate with your collaborator: It includes code, results and steps
2. Supports multiformat outputs such as HTML, PDF, Markdow, websites and more
2. Reproducibility of research

### Open a new Quarto document in Rstudio
Quarto file is a plain text file with `.qmd` extension. To create a new Quarto document:
File > New File > Quarto Document
![](../img/quarto_file_open.png){width="100%" fig-align="center"}
This will open a new window with several options. We can select the Quarto outputs such as 
Documents, Presentation, interactive in different formats. For example, for documents,
we can pick HTML, PDF or Word format. We can even choose Engine Knitr or Jupyter.

![](../img/new_quarto_doc.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"}
This will create an new unamed `Untitled.qmd` file. Lets rename it, by going to File, Save As and name of the file



## Render a Quarto document
Rendering a Quarto document help to convert the .qmd document to the requested format. 
The Quarto document(.qmd) is first processed using the knitr and then converted to the final format using 
pandoc.
![](../img/render.png){width="80%" fig-align="center"}

### Components of Quarto:
1. The YAML header(---)
2. Code chunk (```{r})
3. Text


### YAML header
The header for the Quarto document is written in YAML language. It allows to specify themes,
formats, executable option etc. Additionally, It consists of series of metadata such as
title, author and editor.
![](../img/yaml_header.png){width="80%" fig-align="center"}

Some of the additional contents of the YAML header can be found
[here](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-basics.html)


## Code chunks
Code chunks is a section whetre you can write the code and execute it. 
It is enclosed in a three backticks followed by `r`.

Code chunks can be added in three different ways:

1. Keyboard commands: `Ctrl-Alt-I` (Windows) or `Cmd-Option-I` (Mac)
2. Clicking the insert button
![](../img/insert_code_chunk.png){width="40%" fig-align="center"}
3. Typing it manually
```{r}

```
